## 1. High-Level Business Objective(s)

In Time Tec's objective is to launch a modern, accessible, and mobile-friendly Idaho.gov website that fosters stronger engagement between Idaho's government and its citizens. Through a user-centered design approach and proven AI technology, we will simplify access to essential state information while ensuring the site embodies Idaho's unique brand identity. The new website will meet the evolving needs of users, offering an intuitive experience and robust features that will benefit citizens for years to come. Additionally, the platform will be designed for easy updates and maintenance,

## 2. Project Parameters

## 2.1. Items Out of Scope

The following Services are not included in this SOW:

- Content Creation: ITS will provide the content that is needed for the hi-fidelity mockups, including images, text elements, and other content.
- Custom Chatbot Development: ITT will integrate a commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) chatbot solution; no custom LLM tuning, prompt engineering, or multi-turn conversational design will be performed within the scope of this project.
- Chatbot Support: AI chatbot support is limited to the vendor integration. All support of chatbot availability, functionality, accuracy, and performance is the responsibility of the chatbot vendor and/or ITS.
- Non-Idaho.gov Domains: Content or functionality related to websites outside the *.idaho.gov domain is not included, unless otherwise specified for search indexing.
- Intranet or Internal Tools Integration: integration with internal systems (e.g., employee portals, HR systems, or agency-specific backends) is excluded unless otherwise specified by the solution architecture resultant from the Discovery Phase.

## 2.2. Partner Relationship

- 2.2.1. Developer will adhere to recognized industry standards and best practices in performing Services pursuant to this SOW and commits to deliver high-quality solutions that exceed Customer's expectations.
- 2.2.2. Customer will provide timely feedback on implemented features and ensure that the Developer has access to any required platform environments, as well as internal Customer subject matter experts and key stakeholders, for requirements gathering, design input, and other consultation.

## 2.3. Assumptions and Constraints

- 2.3.1. Scheduling Customer "User" interviews will be subject to the availability of identified Users.
- 2.3.2. The vendor-provided chatbot solution will be selected and procured, and integration instructions or support will be available to the project team by the end of discovery.
- 2.3.3. Project teams will be granted the necessary access to relevant systems at the onset of the engagement.
- 2.3.4. ITS will own responsibility for reviewing, revising, and providing all final content, including any that is migrated, rewritten, or net-new.
- 2.3.5. Delays caused by inaccurate assumptions or other constraints may require an extension to the timeline for performance or require additional resources, which may impact cost.

## Our Approach

Our process for Idaho.gov will leverage ITS's vision for a state-of-the-art website, combining deep research, usercentered design, and industry-leading practices to create a modern, efficient platform. Through Agile development, we'll refine features based on continuous feedback, ensuring alignment with user needs and project goals. Post-launch, we provide support and training to empower ITS for seamless long-term management and success.

![Image](data:image/png;base64,)

## Discovery

## Requirements | Research | Documentation

Our discovery process for Idaho.gov begins by gathering known requirements from internal stakeholders, followed by insights from site analytics, user research, and competitive analysis. A dedicated project sponsor will guide the team in identifying and addressing project risks, including an in-depth exploration of AI search and chat options, along with usability testing with 5-8 users. To modernize the site we will create an updated style tile and style guide for Idaho.gov using a proven collaborative approach to ensure alignment and clarity on its look and feel. Using these guides will then create all high-fidelity designs. We will also provide technical documentation and a detailed project plan, leading to a precise development SOW. This comprehensive process boosts project clarity, quality, and development delivery success rates.

## Development

Agile | Collaborative | Refinement

Development for Idaho.gov will unfold in four phases. First, we will establish the project charter, stories, and development and testing environments. Establishing project plans, expectations, and ceremonies early, according to an Agile framework creates a quick start and smooth experience. Phase 2 will focus on rapidly developing pages and features in accordance with the project plan, requirements, and designs. We will have weekly or bi-monthly demo and feedback sessions with the key stakeholders. Next, we will conduct full-system QA across all features, perform iterative UAT with feedback loops, and address any bugs or refinements. In the final phase we will complete final testing, deploy to the production environment, and implement baseline SEO and Google Analytics to ensure the site meets functionality, usability, and accessibility standards for launch.

## Support &amp; Maintenance

## Training | Optimization

We provide two months of post-launch support to address any issues, defects, or modifications, ensuring all deliverables are promptly resolved. During this period, we offer training on custom features, WordPress admin panel configurations, and any plugins used. This training will also help ITS transition smoothly into supporting the site after the post-launch phase, enhancing their ability to manage and maintain the site effectively.

Implemented IRIS using Microsoft Dynamics 365 to automate and streamline manual processes.

## Accomplishment:

Reduced administrative burden and improved efficiency for both staff and claimants.

![Image](data:image/png;base64,)

The Idaho Industrial Commission (IIC) relied on outdated software and manual processes to manage compliance, benefits, and other key services-resulting in inefficiencies, high costs, and limited flexibility for claimants. To solve this, IIC partnered with In Time Tec to build IRIS (Industrial Commission's Redesigned Information System)-a modern solution to automate workflows, streamline data management, and enhance reporting.

IRIS was brought to life by implementing Microsoft Dynamics 365 along with Microsoft 365 tools such as Power BI, Power Automate, and digital document storage. Using a Rapid Application Development (RAD) approach, we worked closely with the Commission throughout the process to customize features, quickly adapt to changes, and ensure the system met evolving needs. IRIS now provides a modern, efficient, and user-friendly platform that reduces costs, streamlines operations, and empowers both staff and claimants.

## Project Plan

Our objective is to launch a modern, accessible, and mobile-friendly Idaho.gov website that fosters stronger engagement between Idaho's government and its citizens. Through a user-centered design approach and proven AI technology, we will simplify access to essential state information while ensuring the site embodies Idaho's unique brand identity. The new website will meet the evolving needs of users, offering an intuitive experience and robust features that will benefit citizens for years to come. Additionally, the platform will be designed for easy updates and maintenance, reducing long-term costs.

In partnership with ITS, we will deliver a state government website that serves as a model of excellence, offering a userfriendly experience that will inspire and set the benchmark for government websites across Idaho.

## Discovery Stage (14 Weeks)

## Phase 1: Planning &amp; Initial Setup (Week 1-2)

- Project Charter &amp; Kickoff Meeting: Establish SMEs, communication channels, RACI chart and project charter.
- Begin Stakeholder Interviews: Schedule and conduct interviews with key stakeholders to gather detailed business requirements.
- Document Existing Sitemap: Create a complete visual documentation of the existing website sitemap, integrations, and links.
- User Research Plan: Identify 10-15 potential customers and create research methods and plans. (the plan includes interviews with 5-8 users)
- Content Gathering: Begin gathering and documenting existing site content into a shared SharePoint site.

## Phase 2: Research &amp; Analysis (Weeks 3-5)

- Complete Stakeholder Interviews: Finish gathering business requirements.
- Technical Documentation: Gather and document technical requirements and architecture.
- Brand Sprint &amp; Style Creation: Conduct initial brand sprint session to align on vision, voice, styles and goals.
- Document Current Site Analytics: Analyze and document current site usage.
- Document User Flows: Visualize key user flows to identify improvement opportunities.
- Government Site Analysis: Identify 2-4 state government websites and complete comparative analysis.
- Recruit User Interviewees: Contact potential interviewees via email and phone and schedule interview sessions.
- Conduct User Interviews: Conduct 5-8 User Interviews exploring current site usage, card sorting, and new features usability testing.

## Phase 3: Synthesis &amp; Documentation (Weeks 6-7)

- Research Report: Compile findings from customer interviews, site analytics, and comparative analysis into a comprehensive insights report.

- Finalize Updated Brand and Style Guide: Approve updated typography, colors, iconography, and styling for the new site.
- Draft Future Site Map: Draft a future state site map based on research findings.
- Business Requirements: Finalize requirements documentation.
- Technical Research: Document possible technical implementations researched.
- Content Gathering: Finish gathering and documenting existing site content into a shared SharePoint site.

## Phase 4: Hi-Fi Designs &amp; Technical Solutioning (Weeks 8-11)

- High-Fidelity Mockups: Begin designing up to 32 unique page layouts, including navigation and footer redesign, with mobile and desktop responsiveness.
- High-Fidelity Mockup Review &amp; Iteration: Present hi-fidelity designs for review and implement feedback (up to two rounds of iteration).
- Initial SEO Research: Establish foundational SEO keywords and strategy for the new website.
- Solution Architecture Documentation &amp; Diagrams: Document future state diagrams.
- WordPress Mapping: Create WordPress Plugin list and mapping of site functionality to WordPress plugins and custom development.
- Data Documentation: Complete data architecture and diagrams.

## Phase 5: Finalization &amp; Delivery (Weeks 12-14)

- Technical proposal for Website: Submit recommendations for AI search features, chatbot integration strategy, WCAG compliance features, WP build, and migration plan.
- Development SOW and Project Plan: Craft the scope, deliverables, timelines, and cost for Development Phase efforts.
- Content Punchlist: Provide a detailed inventory of all missing and required content elements for the new website.
- Review and Finalize Supplementary Deliverables: Technical documentation, business requirements documentation, research report, and hi-fidelity designs.

## Development Stage (16 Weeks Estimated)

## Phase 1: Planning &amp; Initial Setup (Weeks 1-4)

- Infrastructure &amp; Environments Set Up: Establish development and testing environments.
- Preliminary Web Design Specifications: Finalize initial webpage designs and populate with gathered content.
- AI Specification &amp; Test Cases: Confirm AI search specification and chatbot integration requirements. Collaborate to develop test plans for both.
- Infrastructure &amp; Environments Set Up: Establish development and testing environments.
- Project Planning: Organize project plan, team, and board to track user stories and project progress.

## Phase 2: Web Development &amp; AI Feature Development (Weeks 5-16)

- Develop Webpages: Develop static webpages, navigation, and key features.
- Develop AI Functionality: Build AI-powered search features and integrate vendor-provided chatbot into the website.
- Testing: Start initial iterative testing (Accessibility/Usability).
- Testing: Begin customer UAT validation on website deliverables.

## Phase 3: QA, Testing, &amp; Refinement (Weeks 13-16, Overlapping Phase 2)

- Testing &amp; QA: Conduct full-system QA; functional, usability, and accessibility testing across all features.
- AI Test Cases: Work with ITS to perform UAT on AI search features and chatbot integration.
- UAT Feedback: second round of UAT, incorporating changes and retesting.
- Refinement &amp; Bug Fixes: Address any issues or inconsistencies to ensure the final product meets customer expectations.

## Phase 4: Final Deployment (Weeks 14-16, Overlapping Phase 3)

- Final Testing: Ensure all AI features and webpages meet the expected standards of functionality, usability, and accessibility.
- Deployment: Set up the final deployment environment and push to production.
- Base SEO &amp; Analytics: Perform baseline SEO and Google Analytics set up and configurations.

## Support &amp; Maintenance (Weeks 17-24)

- Training: Conduct training sessions with customers on the completed website and AI features.
- Post-launch Bug Fixes: Dedicated staff will provide remote maintenance and monitoring to quickly address any bugs or issues that arise.
- Minor Modifications &amp; Enhancements: Provide minor improvements to website design, experience, and features per specifications provided by customer.
